pathogen: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (begomovirus), spread by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci
symptoms: New leaves turn pale yellow, curl upward and become small and cupped
Stunted plant, shortened internodes, flowers drop
No spots or rot: the tell-tale is curling of the youngest leaves
Whiteflies visible on the underside of new leaves

severity_cues.early: A few plants with curled new growth
severity_cues.advanced: Many stunted yellow plants, poor fruit set across the field

favorable_conditions: Warm dry seasons with high whitefly pressure, weedy borders and nearby virus sources

treatment.summary: There is no cure for the virus. Control the whitefly, remove infected plants, protect the rest
steps: Uproot and destroy plants showing symptoms, do the round weekly
Control whitefly: spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL at 0.3 ml per litre on seedlings and edges first
Install yellow sticky traps at 10 per acre and keep them sticky
Cover nurseries with 40 to 50 mesh insect-proof net
Keep field borders weed free, they hide whiteflies

products.name: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL
products.label_source: CIB&RC registered label, waiting period 5 days on tomato

organic: Yellow sticky traps and neem oil 1500 ppm at 3 ml per litre against whitefly
Resistant or tolerant varieties for the next planting
Bordered cropland with maize or castor as a whitefly trap crop

source.org: TNAU Agritech Portal, crop protection, tomato diseases
source.title: Tomato: yellow leaf curl virus and whitefly management

safety_notes: Wear gloves, mask and full sleeves while spraying
Do not harvest within 5 days of any insecticide spray
